tradition.name: Portuguese Folk (Música Popular Portuguesa)
tradition.lineage: The regional rural repertoire of mainland Portugal — Minho vira and chula, Beira and Trás-os-Montes dance tunes, Alentejo and Ribatejo song — collected systematically by Michel Giacometti and Fernando Lopes-Graça in the 1960s-70s and revived by Grupo de Acção Cultural and Brigada Victor Jara, marked by fast 6/8 and 2/4 dance metres, women's high open chest singing, adufe square frame-drum patterns, and plucked viola braguesa and cavaquinho accompaniment.

extras.description: Portuguese folk outside fado is overwhelmingly rural, communal and dance-driven: the Minho's whirling vira and chula, Beira Baixa's adufe-accompanied women's songs, bagpipe and drum ranchos in the north-east. Small plucked instruments — viola braguesa, viola campaniça, cavaquinho — supply strummed chordal drive while frame drums and castanets carry the rhythm and singers use a bright, unrounded, high-set chest voice. It sits closer to Galician tradition across the border than to the urban Lisbon guitar tradition.
exemplars: Michel Giacometti / Lopes-Graça Antologia da Música Regional Portuguesa
